answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, delivery risk is the dominant constraint, not just unit cost. Memory_c4 shows that benchmarking against a market quote (here, the low-cost vendor's price) can move the incumbent on both price and terms without the integration/onboarding uncertainty that switching entails (c1, c6 show incumbent stability across cycles and volume-based cost gains). Memory_c2 is the strongest evidence for switching but only speaks to cost and invoicing accuracy, not delivery performance under tight capacity conditions, so I want that record verified before ruling out a switch entirely. Given only one decision fits this cycle and the contract lapses in 14 days, negotiating with the incumbent using the competing quote as leverage targets the cost mandate while preserving delivery continuity; a full vendor switch or second-source addition can be revisited next cycle if renegotiation falls short of the 18% target.
